pricing.usagePolicy: Prices are per blog, before tax. Standard / High / Ultra articles use 1 / 2 / 3 article units. AI work also shares a capacity limit: at exhaustion it pauses until renewal or an explicit top-up, with no automatic overage. Annual plans renew usage monthly.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Straight answers about the trial, AI articles, sources and publishing with Topiqu.

items.q: How does the free trial work?
items.a: Your first eligible blog gets a 14-day Premium trial and 5 article units. Free requires no card. Choosing Pro or Premium during sign-up asks for a card, with the first charge after the trial; you can cancel before then. CUSTOM is paid immediately on confirmation. Further blogs belonging to the same owner start on Free, with no additional trial. Each blog has its own subscription.

items.q: What counts as an AI article?
items.a: Standard / High / Ultra articles use 1 / 2 / 3 article units. Pro includes 50 units/month; Premium and self-service CUSTOM include 100. Auxiliary AI work has separate operation limits and shares AI capacity with articles. At exhaustion new work pauses until renewal or an explicit purchase; there is no automatic overage. Purchased article units never expire and are separate from AI usage top-ups; an active AI plan is required to generate.

items.q: Where does the AI get its facts?
items.a: Topiqu combines live web research with your own knowledge base — notes, PDF and Word files, web pages or a whole sitemap. Private sources shape the text but are never cited publicly; only sources you mark as public can become citations. Before publishing, a review step checks claims against the sources, and the fact-check panel lets you re-check any article.
Only when you turn on automatic publishing. Otherwise every AI draft waits for you to review and edit it, and you can show an AI-content disclosure on the article.

items.q: How do I know whether answers cite me?
items.a: On Premium, Topiqu builds questions from your Search Console queries, articles and reader comments. It regularly checks whether OpenAI answers cite you and where competitors appear. Questions without your citation become article ideas. This is a sample of selected questions, not a record of private conversations.

items.q: Can I publish Topiqu articles on my existing website?
items.a: Yes. Use the hosted Topiqu publication, connect your domain, sync articles into WordPress with the Topiqu Sync plugin, or fetch them through the External API.

testimonials.title: What personal bloggers say about Topiqu
testimonials.description: Gardening, travel, and writing after work. Read how personal bloggers use Topiqu.

personal.name: Petr Novotný
personal.quote: I mostly write in the evenings after work. I often have a topic in mind, but by the time I sit down, I don't feel like writing. With Topiqu, I start with a draft and work through it. Getting started is where it helps me most.

garden.name: Jana Dvořáková
garden.quote: I'm always trying something in the garden and taking photos of what worked. Turning that into an article was harder. Now I put my notes together, get help with the text, and add my own photos. I rewrite some sentences so they sound more like me.

travel.name: Martin Veselý
travel.quote: After a trip, my phone is full of photos and notes about places worth visiting. Topiqu helps me put them in order. The experiences and recommendations are my own, but having an outline makes the article easier to finish.

crafts.name: Lucie Benešová
crafts.role: A blog about making things at home
crafts.quote: I enjoy making things and showing people how I made them. Writing instructions can get confusing because I take some steps for granted. A draft from Topiqu helps me organise the text. Then I go through my photos and fill in what's missing.

beginner.name: Tomáš Kučera
beginner.quote: This is my first blog, so I'm learning as I go. I like being able to prepare an article, edit it a few times, and publish when I'm happy with it. So far, I mostly write for a few friends, but I'm pleased there's something for them to read.
